blurb: A calm, one-dog-at-a-time home grooming salon a short drive north of Royston in Hall Green, Wakefield WF4. IPET-qualified, welfare-first, no kennels, and prices published up front.
metaDescription: Dog grooming for Royston (S71) at a calm one-to-one home salon in Hall Green, Wakefield WF4. IPET-qualified, no kennels, prices shown. Call or WhatsApp Keith.
lead: A 14-minute run north up the A61 through Newmillerdam brings Royston dogs to Keith's K9 Care, a calm, one-to-one home grooming salon in Hall Green — far enough from the high street that your dog gets the room to settle.
body: Royston sits in the S71 4 postcode, off to the south-east of us, which puts it in a different district from the S75 side of Barnsley we also cover. From the village it's roughly 5 miles north — straight up the A61 past Newmillerdam and into Hall Green. About fourteen minutes door to door, with parking right outside on Castle Meadows, so there's no hunting for a space when you arrive.

We pick up a fair few Royston dogs, and the reason is the setup here. This is a home salon that takes one dog at a time. No rows of cages, no other dogs barking through the wall, no rush to get the next one on the table. For a lot of owners coming from a busy commercial salon, that calm is the whole point — particularly for dogs that have found grooming stressful before.

Royston knows its green space. The old Monckton Colliery and coke works ran for the best part of 140 years on the village's eastern edge, and the spoil heap that came with them is now Rabbit Ings Country Park — 160-odd acres of restored grassland, paths and a lake that's become a genuine wildlife haven. The Trans Pennine Trail runs through along the Barnsley Canal bank, and there's Royston Park on Midland Road for a shorter loop. Plenty of walking close to home, which means plenty of muddy coats — handy for us.

Keith is IPET-qualified and trained at Mrs B's Grooming Academy in Leeds. The work covers a full groom (small £40, medium £50, large or doodle £60), a bath and tidy from £30, a puppy's first groom from £25, nail trims and ear cleans from £10, de-matting from £50 and hand stripping from £50. Every price is on the site before you ring, so you know where you stand. To book, call or WhatsApp Keith on 07926 471552 and we'll sort a time that works.

faqs.q: How far is the salon from Royston?
faqs.a: About 5 miles — a fourteen-minute drive north on the A61 through Newmillerdam to Castle Meadows in Hall Green (WF4). You head towards Wakefield rather than into Barnsley. Parking is right outside the door.

faqs.q: Do you cover Royston and the S71 postcode?
faqs.a: Yes. Royston sits in S71 4, and we groom dogs from across that area — Carlton, New Lodge and the surrounding S71 streets. It's a different postcode district from the S75 Barnsley villages we also see, so wherever you are around Royston, you're welcome.

faqs.q: My dog gets walked at Rabbit Ings — can you handle a really matted, muddy coat?
faqs.a: We can. Country-park coats pick up plenty of mud and knots, and de-matting is a service we offer from £50. If the matting is heavy we'll always put your dog's comfort first rather than force a coat that's too far gone — we'll talk you through the options when you arrive.

faqs.q: What are your opening hours and how do I book?
faqs.a: Booking is by appointment, one dog at a time, so the day stays calm. The quickest way to get a slot is to call or WhatsApp Keith on 07926 471552. Let us know your dog's breed and roughly when suits, and we'll find a time.

faqs.q: My dog is nervous or a rescue — will the one-to-one setup help?
faqs.a: That's exactly who it suits best. With only one dog in the salon at a time, there's no noise from other dogs and no pressure to rush. We let nervous and rescue dogs take grooming at their own pace, building up the parts they find harder rather than forcing them.

faqs.q: Why drive up from Royston when there are salons closer in Barnsley?
faqs.a: Mainly the calm. Royston has no shortage of busy high-street salons nearby, but this is a quiet home setup with no kennels and no other dogs around. For owners who'd rather their dog wasn't sat waiting in a cage among a crowd, the short run up the A61 is worth it.
